summary:
We developed PyroScope, a satellite-based wildfire monitoring and data harmonization platform that addresses inconsistencies and missing observations in MODIS and VIIRS hotspot data. The platform combines satellite observations to create a more consistent record of fire activity. Its key features include data harmonization, historical gap reconstruction using calibrated satellite observations, fire event tracking and classification, and anomaly detection to identify unusual fire patterns. It also incorporates AI-based forecasting to estimate potential hotspot activity over the next 1–7 days, alongside uncertainty analysis to communicate prediction reliability. An interactive dashboard presents hotspot locations, historical trends, reconstructed data, forecasts, and early warnings.

PyroScope addresses the challenge by improving the continuity, consistency, and usability of satellite fire observations. It is important because more reliable fire information can help researchers, environmental agencies, and disaster-management teams monitor wildfire activity and make better-informed decisions.
details:
PyroScope – AI-Powered Satellite Fire Intelligence and Early Warning Platform

PyroScope is an AI-powered platform designed to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire observations and provide a more consistent understanding of fire activity. Using NASA FIRMS datasets, it processes satellite hotspot data through data harmonization, gap reconstruction, fire event tracking, historical analysis, anomaly detection and machine-learning-based forecasting. It estimates hotspot activity over the next 1–7 days and presents the results through an interactive dashboard featuring hotspot maps, historical trends, sensor comparisons, forecasts and a burning activity calendar. The prototype has been developed and tested using satellite hotspot datasets for Punjab, India.

PyroScope helps users understand historical fire patterns, identify unusual activity and make more informed monitoring and preparedness decisions. Its intended impact is to support forest departments, disaster management authorities, researchers and local communities through accessible satellite-based fire intelligence. Future improvements include expanding geographical coverage, integrating with government agencies, incorporating additional satellite and weather data, and providing location-based alerts to residents and industries in high-risk regions.

The project uses NASA FIRMS, MODIS and VIIRS datasets, Python for data processing and machine learning, and XGBoost for hotspot forecasting, along with web development and visualisation technologies. Its creativity lies in combining satellite data harmonization, historical gap estimation, AI-based forecasting and uncertainty analysis into a single platform rather than simply displaying fire hotspots. During development, the team considered satellite differences, data reliability, historical continuity, prediction uncertainty, regional applicability and practical usability.
